problem_statement: The Codrops InteractiveLandscape project is a no-build static three.js WebGL demo with three HTML routes (index.html/index2.html/index3.html), a full-viewport animated terrain rendered onto an absolutely-positioned landscape surface, and four local shader palette textures under img/ (pallete5/pallete6/pallete/pallete_bw). The demo's own interactive control is a Palette atlas panel mounted in the normal-flow .content of every route: four swatch buttons repaint the live terrain by swapping the three.js shader texture, and a live readout reports 'Now painting: <label> · palette N of 4'. The current build has four defects to repair so the panel behaves and reads correctly on every route and breakpoint: (1) on a 390px mobile viewport the swatch row is a rigid fixed-width nowrap line whose swatches never shrink, so the panel forces the document into horizontal overflow; (2) the panel is only mounted on some routes, so demo 2 and/or demo 3 are missing the Palette atlas entirely; (3) the swatch grid collapses on desktop — the swatches shingle over each other via negative margins into a colliding, dark-on-dark illegible pile with the readout buried; (4) clicking a swatch moves the highlight and repaints the terrain but the readout is frozen on the first palette instead of updating to the chosen one. Repair the Palette atlas so: the swatch row wraps and the panel fits a 390px viewport with no horizontal overflow; the panel renders on all three demo routes; the swatches lay out cleanly and legibly; and clicking a swatch updates the readout to the selected palette and count. Do not change the WebGL terrain, the Article/GitHub/Previous demo links, the demo 1/2/3 navigation, the Upgrade title or the Version 5.5 subtitle, and keep the no-build static serving.
required_content: The Palette atlas panel renders in the normal-flow .content of index.html, index2.html AND index3.html (not just one route); its title 'Palette atlas' is present on every demo route.

At a 390px mobile viewport the Palette atlas swatch row wraps and the panel produces no horizontal overflow (tolerance 24px); it must not rely on a blanket overflow-x:hidden that clips honest content.
On desktop the four swatches lay out side by side without overlapping or shingling, and the panel text (heading, readout, swatch labels) is legible against the panel background.
Clicking a swatch repaints the live terrain AND updates the readout to 'Now painting: <selected label> · palette <n> of 4' for the chosen swatch (not a frozen first-palette string).
The animated WebGL terrain, the Article/GitHub/Previous demo links, the demo 1/2/3 navigation, the Upgrade title and the Version 5.5 subtitle remain present and reachable on every route.
design_constraints: Preserve the demo's dark full-viewport aesthetic, Barlow type, coral (--color-link) accent and the fixed frame chrome; only the Palette atlas panel layout, presence and readout wiring change.
Do not remove, hide or restyle the WebGL terrain surface to mask overflow; it is absolutely positioned and is not the overflow source.
Do not use a blanket overflow-x:hidden on the row/body to hide overflow — the honest content right-edge must fit the 390px viewport.
Keep the change inside the Palette atlas layer (css/palette-atlas.css + js/palette-atlas.js + the per-route panel markup); base.css and the vendored scene JS stay identical across legs.
state_constraints: desktop_initial / desktop_atlas capture index.html at 1440px with the Palette atlas in view; desktop_demo2 / desktop_demo3 capture the other two routes at 1440px.
tablet_initial captures index.html at 834px and mobile_atlas captures index.html at 390px, where the un-repaired swatch row overflows the viewport.
palette_pick clicks the pallete6 swatch on index.html at 1440px; on a correct build the readout updates to 'Now painting: pallete6 ridge · palette 2 of 4', on a frozen build it stays on palette 1.
Source inspection confirms a no-build static three.js demo whose leg-varying files are css/palette-atlas.css, js/palette-atlas.js and the per-route panel markup.

change_completion: The Palette atlas panel is present on all three demo routes with its title and swatches.
Clicking a swatch updates the live readout to the selected palette label and index, and the WebGL terrain repaints.
design_consistency: The panel keeps its dark translucent styling, Barlow type and coral active-swatch accent; swatches sit cleanly side by side and text is legible.
The fixed frame chrome, demo navigation and the WebGL terrain look identical to the original across every route.
regression: All three demo routes serve statically and remain reachable with the demo 1/2/3 links intact.
The animated WebGL terrain still renders on every route and the Upgrade / Version 5.5 copy is unchanged.
responsive: 390px mobile index.html has no horizontal overflow (tolerance 24px); the swatches wrap rather than forcing a scroll.
834px tablet index.html also fits without horizontal overflow and the panel reflows cleanly at both breakpoints.

author_notes: Repo-grounded L4 task on the no-build static three.js WebGL InteractiveLandscape demo. The native lever is the demo's OWN Palette atlas control panel (swatch buttons that swap the live terrain shader texture plus a 'Now painting' readout), placed in normal flow inside .content so it is the sole normal-flow chrome (the terrain surface is absolutely positioned and never drives document overflow). Four orthogonal gates run through this one panel: no_horizontal_overflow at 390px (baseline fixed 720px nowrap swatch row overflows ~366px; a shallow non-fix keeps a rigid min-width:600px nowrap line with overflow-x:hidden on an inner wrapper only and still overflows ~246px), cross-route dom_assertions on the panel title (present on all three demo routes in the reference; the defective legs omit it on demo 2 and/or demo 3), visual_regression on the desktop panel (the broken leg shingles the swatches via large negative margins into a colliding near-black-on-near-black illegible pile with the readout buried) and interaction_assertions on the swatch click (the broken leg freezes the readout on the first palette while the highlight and terrain still change). Barlow fonts were vendored locally and the remote font link dropped (build INFRA identical across legs) so console/network stay clean; headless swiftshader WebGL warnings are ignored by the console-error gate. Uses local img/pallete*.png shader textures and a canvas visual surface.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: codrops/InteractiveLandscape is a runnable no-build static three.js WebGL demo whose own Palette atlas swatch control (repaints the live terrain shader texture) is an ideal native interactive lever for a four-gate L4 task carried entirely by that normal-flow HUD panel.
